- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% in early horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2.5), model often overcorrects with exaggerated downward momentum; cap forecast decline to 1.5x the prior day’s drop.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show price > 2.10, forecast should not exceed 2.20 unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- Forecast horizon 1–7 days: model is overly optimistic; apply 15–25% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Forecast horizon 8–30 days: model often overestimates volatility; apply 20–30% downward adjustment if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.33, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to misread trend direction; align forecast with sentiment’s most recent dominant polarity.
